sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Fairmont Ground, hold short of runway 09.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, after departure fly heading 350, cleared for takeoff runway 09, traffic is a Cessna on base.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, descend to flight level 180, reduce speed to 250 knots, contact Kingsley Approach on 127.85.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Ravenna Airport via the NAVIO ONE departure, maintain 4,000, departure frequency 121.9, squawk 5146.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: You are descending into Kingsley and you are now passing flight level 120. The transition level is below you, so a new pressure setting is coming. Now ATC contacts you. Acknowledge the instruction and report your present altitude.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Kingsley Approach, descend to 6,000, QNH 1008, transition level 70.

On short final into Fairmont you saw a small drone hovering about two hundred feet above the ground, just left of the runway threshold. You were too busy to report it then. You have now landed and the ground controller calls you. Acknowledge the taxi instruction and report what you saw during the approach.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Fairmont Ground, taxi to the gate via Charlie.

Centre instructed you to maintain 290 knots for separation. At your present weight and altitude 290 knots leaves you no buffet margin, so you reduced to 270 knots and you are flying at 270 now. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining 290 knots?
270 knots / buffet margin

You are being vectored for the approach and you are twelve miles from QUILL at 9,000 feet. Your descent calculation shows that you cannot lose that much height before QUILL without exceeding your descent rate limits. Listen to the controller, make a readback of what you can accept, and a request with a reason.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 4,000, cross QUILL at 4,000.
Delivery gave you squawk 3027 before departure. You set 3207 in the transponder by mistake and it has been running that way since take-off. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, verify your squawk.

Your clearance includes the SELDO transition. Your flight management computer holds two points called SELDO and you are not sure which one is on your route, and the crossing altitude on your chart does not match the one in the computer. You are level at flight level 310. Contact Westlake Control. Verify which waypoint is on your route, and request the crossing altitude.
SELDO

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying HL123, which goes through 3 flight stages: Clearance, Taxi, Departure.

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123 at Fairmont Airport, bound for Kingsley. Boarding is complete and you are ready to copy your clearance. It is a cold morning and the ground crew has reported light frost on the wings.

body.text: Contact Fairmont Delivery and request your clearance.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Kingsley Airport via the BRAVA TWO departure, SELDO transition, climb and maintain 7,000, departure frequency 126.4, squawk 3027.
Listen to the controller's message, respond accordingly and advise what you need before departure.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, readback is correct, your slot time is 0845, and the ground crew reports light frost on the upper wing surfaces.
de-icing required

pre.text: Situation Update De-icing is complete and the ground crew has cleared you off the pad. Your slot has moved back and you have not been told the new time. You are holding short of taxiway Delta.

body.text: Contact Fairmont Ground, request taxi and inquire about your new slot time.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, runway 09, taxi via Delta and Foxtrot, hold short of runway 14, give way to the Bombardier CRJ on Foxtrot.
Listen to the controller's question and respond accordingly. Tell him what you need to know before you can answer.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, the CRJ ahead of you is going to be a while sorting out a paperwork problem. If you can take an intersection departure from Foxtrot I can get you out ahead of him — can you work with that?

pre.text: Situation Update You have checked the performance figures and the distance from Foxtrot is enough for today's weight. You are now holding short of runway 09 at Foxtrot.

body.text: Listen to the tower and give a full readback.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Fairmont Tower, wind 080 at 11, line up and wait runway 09 at Foxtrot, number one.
Listen to the tower and give a full readback. Then advise that you are ready for an immediate departure.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, traffic is a Cessna Caravan on a three mile final, cleared for immediate takeoff runway 09 at Foxtrot, no delay.

pre.text: Situation Update You are airborne and climbing through 2,500 feet on the BRAVA TWO departure.

body.text: Contact Fairmont Departure and report your passing altitude.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback. Then request the information you are missing.

body.label: Departure
body.text: HL123, Fairmont Departure, radar contact, climb and maintain flight level 190, cleared direct SELDO.
SELDO crossing altitude not on the chart

Follow-up question: You have just finished Task A, as the pilot of Hotel Lima one two three. In this situation, you accepted an intersection departure instead of waiting for the full runway. What did you have to check before you accepted it, and why did you ask the controller what you asked? In your role as a pilot, when would you refuse an intersection departure? Give an example.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, descending through flight level 200 for 8,000, inbound to Thornbury Airport. You have information Kilo.

body.text: Contact Thornbury Approach and report your position.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Thornbury Approach, good morning, descend and maintain 8,000, reduce speed to 230 knots, expect the ILS runway 27, Thornbury altimeter 30.12.

pre.text: Situation Update Levelling off at 8,000 you notice that the captain's and the first officer's airspeed indications differ by about twenty knots, and the standby indicator does not agree with either of them.

body.text: Inform the controller of your situation, state that you are maintaining 8,000, and request a groundspeed readout from his radar.
Listen to the controller's response, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, I show your groundspeed 290, fly heading 240 and maintain 8,000, and say your intentions.
Listen to the controller and respond negatively with a reason. Request what you need instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, I have a Boeing 737 closing from behind — are you able to give me 250 knots or better? If not I will have to turn you off.

pre.text: Situation Update You have finished the checklist. The captain's indications now agree with the groundspeed the controller gave you, but you will have to fly the approach manually and you cannot use autoland.

body.text: Contact approach, give them an update of your situation and state what you will need for the approach.
Listen to the controller and respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, I have to change your approach. The ILS 27 glide path is out for calibration, so the best I can do is the RNAV 27. Weather is fine, ceiling 4,000 broken.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, turn right heading 300, descend and maintain 3,000 until established, cleared for the RNAV runway 27 approach, contact Thornbury Tower on 118.1.
Listen to the controller's question and provide the requested information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the tower wants to know whether you need the emergency services out, or whether a normal landing is fine.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK C. Reporting about Task B

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
